issue_context.title: Error for importing ModuleWithProviders into @Component.imports could be improved
issue_context.body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

compiler

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

Using `RouterModule.forRoot([...])` in standalone's component imports results in errors that are not immediately actionable. This is a pretty common scenario since people trying out "standalone" will try to move router's configuration _somewhere_ and many will try moving the `RouterModule.forRoot([...])` into `@Component.imports`., ex.:

```typescript
@Component({
  selector: 'app-root',
  template: `
   ....
  `,
  standalone: true,
  imports: [RouterModule.forRoot([])],
})
export class AppRoot {
}
```

Trying to do the above will result in the 2 following errors:

```
Error: src/main.ts:25:12 - error NG1010: 'imports' must be an array of components, directives, pipes, or NgModules
  Value is of type '[(not statically analyzable)]'.

25   imports: [RouterModule.forRoot([])],
              ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


Error: src/main.ts:25:13 - error TS2322: Type 'ModuleWithProviders<RouterModule>' is not assignable to type 'any[] | Type<any>'.

25   imports: [RouterModule.forRoot([])],
               ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
``` 

Things that might be confusing to the users:
* `(not statically analyzable)` might be cryptic and not-actionable
* the second error actually gets us a bit more info since it indicates that `ModuleWithProviders` don't "fit" into the `@Component.imports` "slot"

Not sure if we can improve things on the compiler side, especially for the first error. 

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
v14
```

review_comments:
super-nit: this test is great from the long-term maintainability point of view as it doesn't duplicate the error message (so it won't break when the error message changes). For a reviewer, though, it is hard to see the full error message and judge the user experience.

Probably hard to get both but yeh, would love to see somewhere the full error message as reported to a user...
Good point, I agree; I've added message assertions for these tests.

I actually agree with the first part of Pawel's statement - including specific error messages in the test assertion adds a lot of brittleness and we should not do that.

A good compromise and a good best practice in general would be to include an example of the error experience in the commit message itself. An easy way to generate this is to temporarily replace `env.driveDiagnostics()` with `env.driveMain()` and copy-paste the resulting diagnostic in its context.

I am a bit torn on this, as capturing the exact error message can be valuable to verify that substitutions and formatting is as expected. It's quite easy to inadvertently get `[object Object]` in a message somewhere or to get incorrect punctuation when there's conditions involved (e.g. 3ebf9e7442205ef778da2589d51e4abab3a597bd).

In general I'd prefer "golden"-like test assertions, where we compare the output against a golden/snapshot file and have ways of auto updating such snapshots. This is how e.g. TypeScript and esbuild author most of their tests.

That said, removed the message for now.
